*The objective of this script is to (i) train the Sr isotope time series model, (ii) train the trace element model, (iii) combine the predictions, and (iv) evaluate the classification performance using out-of-sample test set.*

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls()) #clean the environment

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(ranger)

# plotting
```

# Load data

Read in baseline known-origin juvenile Sr isotope time series dataset.
Note that this Sr data has been splined and also includes synthetic fry migrant data.

```{r}
# read in full isoscape data for Sr isotope time series model
iso_full_read <- read_csv(here('data','ref_data_for_model_2025-09-16.csv'))

# modify columns
iso_full <- iso_full_read %>% 
  rename(lab_id = Sample_ID) %>% 
  mutate(NAT_LOC = factor(NAT_LOC)) %>% 
  
  # assign real and synthetic
  mutate(type = case_when(
    grepl("Fish", lab_id) ~ "synthetic",
    TRUE ~ "real")) %>% 
  mutate(HvW = case_when(
    NAT_LOC %in% c("CNH", "FEH", "MEH", "NIH", "MOH") ~ "H",
    TRUE ~ "W")) %>% 
  
  # drop rows with NA in columns starting with "X"
  filter(if_all(starts_with("X"), ~ !is.na(.)))

# sample size per natal source
iso_full %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC, type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>% 
  knitr::kable(format = "simple", caption = "Sample size of the full dataset of known-origin juveniles by natal source and type.")

glimpse(iso_full)

# sample size per source
iso_full %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC, type) %>% 
  tally()

# check any missing data for all columns - no missing values
iso_full %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_missing)) %>% 
  print(n = 100)

```

# Training and test set creation

1. Identify overlapping samples between Sr isotope and TE baseline - n = 71

```{r}
# overlapping samples n = 71 samples overlapping between isoscape and TE baseline
overlap_ids <- intersect(iso_full$lab_id, te_full$lab_id)

iso_overlap <- iso_full %>% filter(lab_id %in% overlap_ids)
te_overlap  <- te_full %>% filter(lab_id %in% overlap_ids)
```

2. Now create a balanced test set from overlapping samples that includes measurements for Sr isotope and TE.

```{r}
# pick (say) n = 5 per source, or the min available across sources
#n_per_source <- min(table(te_overlap$NAT_LOC))
n_per_source <- 5

# balanced sample
set.seed(123)
test_te <- te_overlap %>%
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>%
  slice_sample(n = n_per_source) %>%
  ungroup()

test_iso <- iso_overlap %>%
  filter(lab_id %in% test_te$lab_id)
```

3. Add Sr isotope only test sample from the other 12 sources

```{r}
te_sources <- unique(te_full$NAT_LOC)
iso_only <- iso_full %>% filter(!NAT_LOC %in% te_sources)

# sample e.g. 5 per additional source
n_iso_only <- 5

set.seed(123)
test_iso_extra <- iso_only %>%
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>%
  slice_sample(n = n_iso_only) %>%
  ungroup()
```

4. Combine test sets and create training data

```{r}
# full iso test set (5 shared + extra sources) 5 samples per source N = 85
test_iso_all <- bind_rows(test_iso, test_iso_extra)

# training sets = all minus holdout
train_iso <- iso_full %>% filter(!lab_id %in% test_iso_all$lab_id)
train_te  <- te_full %>% filter(!lab_id %in% test_te$lab_id)

# save test sets
write.csv(test_te,here('outputs',paste0("test_te_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")), row.names = F)
write.csv(test_iso_all, here('outputs',paste0("test_iso_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")), row.names = F)
```

# Sr isotope time series

Now train the Sr time series model

## Balance sample

```{r}
# create a balanced sample size per natal source (also balanced real and synthetic per natal source)
# estimate the target sample size per natal source for "real" samples
target_size_real <- train_iso %>% 
  filter(type == "real") %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>% 
  tally() %>% 
  summarise(target = round(mean(n, na.rm = T))) %>% 
  pull(target)

# the target sample size per source was based on the mean size across sources
# this is a balanced approach - upsampling WITH replacement for small sources and downsampling WITHOUT replacement for large sources
target_size_real

# sample size before resampling
train_iso %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC, type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>% 
  print(n = 100)

# Separate the real and simulated rows
real_data <- train_iso %>% filter(type == "real")
syn_data  <- train_iso %>% filter(type != "real")

# Resample only the "real" rows by NAT_LOC
# resample to n = 40 for W and n = 60 for H (since hatchery source does not release fry and thus no fake fry needed)
set.seed(1234)
real_data_resampled <- real_data %>%
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map_df(~ {
    n_group <- nrow(.x)
    sample_size <- ifelse(unique(.x$HvW) == "H", 60, 40) # 60 for H and 40 for W

    if (n_group < sample_size) {
      slice_sample(.x, n = sample_size, replace = TRUE)  # Upsample
    } else {
      slice_sample(.x, n = sample_size, replace = FALSE) # Downsample
    }
  })

# resample "synthetic" to n = 20
set.seed(1234)
syn_data_resampled <- syn_data %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>% 
  slice_sample(n = 20, replace = TRUE)

# Bind the resampled real data with the original simulated data
train_iso_rs <- bind_rows(real_data_resampled, syn_data_resampled)

# sample size after resampling - n = 60 per source
train_iso_rs %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC, type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>% 
  knitr::kable(format = "simple", caption = "Sample size of the training dataset of known-origin juveniles by natal source and type.")
```

## Model tuning and training

Note that this is fitting the full Sr time series model (not loop model)

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# -----------------------------------
# 1. Define predictors and outcome
# -----------------------------------
predictors <- c(
  paste0("X", seq(100, 320, 10)), # X100, X110, ... X320
  "mean_exog"
)

# -----------------------------------
# 2. Recipe
# -----------------------------------
iso_recipe <- recipe(NAT_LOC ~ X100 + X110 + X120 + X130 + X140 + X150 + X160 + X170 + X180 + X190 + 
        X200 + X210 + X220 + X230 + X240 + X250 + X260 + X270 + X280 + X290 + 
        X300 + X310 + X320 + mean_exog, data = train_iso_rs) 

# -----------------------------------
# 3. Model specification
# -----------------------------------
rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  mtry  = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  trees = 1000
) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# -----------------------------------
# 4. Workflow
# -----------------------------------
rf_wflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(iso_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)

# -----------------------------------
# 5. Resampling (CV folds)
# -----------------------------------
iso_folds <- vfold_cv(train_iso_rs, v = 10, strata = NAT_LOC)

# -----------------------------------
# 6. Tuning grid
# -----------------------------------
rf_grid <- grid_regular(
  mtry(range = c(2, length(predictors))),  
  min_n(range = c(2, 20)),                  
  levels = 10
)

# -----------------------------------
# 7. Tune the model
# -----------------------------------
rf_tune_res <- tune_grid(
  rf_wflow,
  resamples = iso_folds,
  grid      = rf_grid,
  metrics   = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::accuracy, yardstick::kap),
  control   = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

# -----------------------------------
# 8. Select best parameters
# -----------------------------------
best_rf <- select_best(rf_tune_res, metric = "accuracy")

# -----------------------------------
# 9. Finalize workflow
# -----------------------------------
final_rf_wflow <- finalize_workflow(rf_wflow, best_rf)

# -----------------------------------
# 10. Fit final model
# -----------------------------------
final_rf_fit <- fit(final_rf_wflow, data = train_iso_rs)

# -----------------------------------
# 11. Save final model as RDS
# -----------------------------------
saveRDS(final_rf_fit, file = here('outputs',paste0("final_sr_ts_model_", Sys.Date(), ".rds")))

# -----------------------------------
# 12. Test-set evaluation
# -----------------------------------
rf_test_pred <- predict(final_rf_fit, new_data = test_iso_all, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(predict(final_rf_fit, new_data = test_iso_all)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_iso_all %>% select(NAT_LOC))

# Accuracy and Kappa
metrics <- rf_test_pred %>% 
  metrics(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class)

# Confusion matrix
conf_mat_res <- rf_test_pred %>%
  conf_mat(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class)

# Print results
print(metrics)
print(conf_mat_res)

```

# TE model

Now train the trace element RF model

## Balance sample
Similar to the Sr isotope model, balance the training data

```{r}
glimpse(train_te)

# compute sample size per source
source_counts <- train_te %>%
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

source_counts

# target sample size = median - n = 13
target_n <- median(source_counts$n)

# function to balance each group
balance_group <- function(df, target_n) {
  n_current <- nrow(df)
  
  if(n_current < target_n) {
    # upsample with replacement
    df <- df %>% slice_sample(n = target_n, replace = TRUE)
  } else if(n_current > target_n) {
    # downsample without replacement
    df <- df %>% slice_sample(n = target_n, replace = FALSE)
  }
  # if equal, do nothing
  return(df)
}

# apply to each NAT_LOC
train_te_rs <- train_te %>%
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>%
  group_modify(~balance_group(.x, target_n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# check counts
train_te_rs %>% count(NAT_LOC)

```

## Model tuning and training

```{r}
train_te_rs

set.seed(123)

train_te_rs

# -----------------------------------
# 2. Recipe
# -----------------------------------
te_recipe <- recipe(NAT_LOC ~ Sr_Ca + Ba_Ca, data = train_te_rs) 

# -----------------------------------
# 3. Model specification
# -----------------------------------
rf_spec_te <- rand_forest(
  mtry  = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  trees = 1000
) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# -----------------------------------
# 4. Workflow
# -----------------------------------
rf_wflow_te <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(te_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec_te)

# -----------------------------------
# 5. Resampling (CV folds)
# -----------------------------------
te_folds <- vfold_cv(train_te_rs, v = 10, strata = NAT_LOC)

# -----------------------------------
# 6. Tuning grid
# -----------------------------------
rf_grid_te <- grid_regular(
  mtry(range = c(1, 2)),  
  min_n(range = c(2, 20)),                  
  levels = 10
)

# -----------------------------------
# 7. Tune the model
# -----------------------------------
rf_tune_res_te <- tune_grid(
  rf_wflow_te,
  resamples = te_folds,
  grid      = rf_grid_te,
  metrics   = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::accuracy, yardstick::kap),
  control   = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

# -----------------------------------
# 8. Select best parameters
# -----------------------------------
best_rf_te <- select_best(rf_tune_res_te, metric = "accuracy")

# -----------------------------------
# 9. Finalize workflow
# -----------------------------------
final_rf_wflow_te <- finalize_workflow(rf_wflow_te, best_rf_te)

# -----------------------------------
# 10. Fit final model
# -----------------------------------
final_rf_fit_te <- fit(final_rf_wflow_te, data = train_te_rs)

# -----------------------------------
# 11. Save final model as RDS
# -----------------------------------
saveRDS(final_rf_fit_te, file = here('outputs',paste0("final_te_model_", Sys.Date(), ".rds")))

# -----------------------------------
# 12. Test-set evaluation
# -----------------------------------
rf_test_pred_te <- predict(final_rf_fit_te, new_data = test_te, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(predict(final_rf_fit_te, new_data = test_te)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_te %>% select(NAT_LOC))

# Accuracy and Kappa
metrics_te <- rf_test_pred_te %>% 
  metrics(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class)

# Confusion matrix
conf_mat_res_te <- rf_test_pred_te %>%
  conf_mat(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class)

# Print results
print(metrics_te)
print(conf_mat_res_te)

# look at the list of the best candidate models
show_best(rf_tune_res_te, metric = "accuracy", n = 10)

```

Confusion matrix for strontium time series model

```{r}
cm <- conf_mat(ts_pred, truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_ts) %>% 
   pluck("table") %>%
  as_tibble()

    group_by(Truth) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n),
           label = paste0(n, "\n(", scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1), ")")) %>%
    mutate(Truth = factor(Truth, levels = c("SAC", "CNH", "BAT", "MIL", "DEE", "BUT", "FEA", "FEH", "YUB", "AME", "NIH", "MOK", "MOH", "STA", "TUO", "MER", "MEH"))) %>% 
  mutate(Prediction = factor(Prediction, levels = c("MEH", "MER", "TUO", "STA", "MOH", "MOK", "NIH", "AME", "YUB", "FEH", "FEA", "BUT", "DEE", "MIL", "BAT", "CNH", "SAC"))) %>% 
  ungroup()

cm_plot <- ggplot(cm_labeled, aes(x = Truth, y = Prediction, fill = prop)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    #geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(Prop, accuracy = 0.1)), color = "white", size = 4) + # percentage
    #geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", prop)), color = "white", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") + # proportion
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
    labs(title = "Confusion matrix of Sr isotope time series model",
         subtitle = paste0("Updated: ", Sys.Date()),
         fill = "Proportion") +
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(legend.position = "none")

cm_plot
```

## TE model

Natal assignment using the TE model

```{r}
final_rf_fit_te <- readRDS(here('outputs','final_te_model_2025-11-06.rds'))

final_rf_fit_te

# read in test data
test_te <- read.csv(here('outputs','test_te_2025-11-06.csv'))

glimpse(test_te)

# check sample size per source
test_te %>% 
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>% 
  tally()

# predict!
set.seed(1234)
te_pred <- test_te %>% 
  bind_cols(predict(final_rf_fit_te, ., type = "class"),
            predict(final_rf_fit_te, ., type = "prob")) %>% 
  
  # rename .pred* columns by appending "_te"
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_te_raw"), starts_with(".pred"))

glimpse(te_pred)
```

Now combine the posterior probs

```{r}
#Set which sources to consider for the model
sources <- c("BAT","DEE","MIL","SAC","BUT","CNH")

# Merge the two prediction tables
test_combined <- ts_pred %>%
  dplyr::select(lab_id, NAT_LOC, starts_with(".pred_"), starts_with("X"), mean_exog) %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub("_ts$", "_sr", .x)) %>%   # rename Sr preds
  left_join(
    te_pred %>%
      dplyr::select(lab_id, starts_with(".pred_"), Sr_Ca, Ba_Ca) %>%
      rename_with(~ gsub("_te_raw$", "_te", .x)), 
    by = "lab_id"
  )

glimpse(test_combined)

# Use te_missing_if_any = TRUE  => fallback to Sr if ANY of the TE probs are NA
# Use te_missing_if_any = FALSE => fallback only if ALL TE probs are NA
te_missing_if_any <- TRUE

# ---- compute posteriors----
test_post <- test_combined %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # grab sr and te vectors for the chosen sources as list-columns
    sr_vec = list(c_across(all_of(paste0(".pred_", sources, "_sr")))),
    te_vec = list(c_across(all_of(paste0(".pred_", sources, "_te")))),
    
    # decide whether the TE prediction should be considered missing
    te_missing = if (te_missing_if_any) any(is.na(unlist(te_vec))) else all(is.na(unlist(te_vec))),
    
    # normalize sr probs (guard against zero / all-NA)
    sr_sum = sum(unlist(sr_vec), na.rm = TRUE),
    sr_norm = list(
      if (is.na(sr_sum) || sr_sum == 0) rep(1/length(unlist(sr_vec)), length(unlist(sr_vec)))
      else unlist(sr_vec) / sr_sum
    ),
    
    # compute raw posterior = sr_norm * te_vec, but only when TE is present
    post_raw = list(
      if (te_missing) rep(NA_real_, length(unlist(sr_vec))) 
      else unlist(sr_norm) * unlist(te_vec)
    ),
    
    # normalize posterior
    post_sum = sum(unlist(post_raw), na.rm = TRUE),
    post_norm = list(
      if (is.na(post_sum) || post_sum == 0) rep(NA_real_, length(unlist(sr_vec)))
      else unlist(post_raw) / post_sum
    ),
    
   # final class with fallback
    .pred_class_final = if (te_missing || all(is.na(unlist(post_norm)))) {
      .pred_class_sr
    } else {
      # if sr_class is NOT one of the allowed sources, stick with sr_class
      if (!(.pred_class_sr %in% sources)) {
        .pred_class_sr
      } else {
        sources[which.max(unlist(post_norm))]
      }
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    post_norm_named = map(post_norm, ~ set_names(as.numeric(.x), paste0("post_norm_post", sources)))
  ) %>%
  unnest_wider(post_norm_named) %>%
  dplyr::select(-sr_vec, -te_vec, -sr_sum, -post_raw, -post_sum, -post_norm)

# example rows where TE was missing and fallback applied
test_post %>% filter(te_missing) %>% dplyr::select(lab_id, NAT_LOC, .pred_class_sr, .pred_class_te, .pred_class_final) %>% head(10)

# finalize probabilities 
test_final <- test_post %>%
  
  relocate(.pred_class_final, .after = .pred_class_te) %>% 
  relocate(.pred_class_sr, .before = .pred_class_te) %>%
  
  # calculate maximum sr ts model prob
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(max_prob_ts = max(c_across(.pred_AME_sr:.pred_YUB_sr)),
         max_prob_te = max(c_across(.pred_BAT_te:.pred_SAC_te)),
         max_prob_final = max(c_across(post_norm_postBAT:post_norm_postCNH))) %>% 
  
  # relocate
  relocate(max_prob_ts, .before = .pred_class_sr) %>% 
  relocate(max_prob_te, .after = max_prob_ts) %>% 
  relocate(max_prob_final, .after = max_prob_te) %>% 
  
   # make factor ordering consistent
  mutate(
    .pred_class_sr    = factor(.pred_class_sr,    levels = source_order),
    .pred_class_te    = factor(.pred_class_te,    levels = source_order),
    .pred_class_final = factor(.pred_class_final, levels = source_order),
    NAT_LOC = factor(NAT_LOC, levels = source_order)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()
  
glimpse(test_final)
```

## Validation

Using the test set, validate how combining the two predictions improved classification accuracy.

```{r}
# final accuracy improved substantially!
# Overall accuracy (only for the six sources)
# sr isotope ts: 0.53
# TE: 0.7
# combined: 0.87

test_final %>% 
  # filter only the sources of interest
  filter(te_missing == FALSE) %>% 
  
  summarise(accuracy_ts = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_sr),
            accuracy_te = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_te),
            accuracy_final = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_final),
            n = n())

# by source
test_final %>% 
  
  # filter only the sources
  filter(te_missing == FALSE) %>% 
  
  group_by(NAT_LOC) %>% 
  
  summarise(accuracy_ts = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_sr),
            accuracy_te = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_te),
            accuracy_final = yardstick::accuracy_vec(truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = .pred_class_final),
            n = n())
```

## Confusion matrix

Look at the confusion matrices for all sources

```{r}
# function to build a CM plot
make_cm_plot <- function(data, pred_col, title){
  cm <- conf_mat(data, truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = !!sym(pred_col)) %>% 
    pluck("table") %>%
    as_tibble()

  cm_lab <- cm %>%
    group_by(Truth) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n),
           label = paste0(n, "\n(", scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1), ")")) %>%
    mutate(Truth = factor(Truth, levels = c("SAC", "CNH", "BAT", "MIL", "DEE", "BUT", "FEA", "FEH",
                                            "YUB", "AME", "NIH", "MOK", "MOH", "STA", "TUO", "MER", "MEH"))) %>% 
    mutate(Prediction = factor(Prediction, levels = c("MEH", "MER", "TUO", "STA", "MOH", "MOK", "NIH",
                                                      "AME", "YUB", "FEH", "FEA", "BUT", "DEE", "MIL", "BAT", "CNH", "SAC"))) %>% 
    ungroup()

  ggplot(cm_lab, aes(x = Truth, y = Prediction, fill = prop)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.0, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
    labs(title = title, fill = "Proportion") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

# Generate the three CMs
cm_sr    <- make_cm_plot(test_final, ".pred_class_sr", "Sr isotope time series")
cm_te    <- make_cm_plot(test_final, ".pred_class_te", "TE model")
cm_final <- make_cm_plot(test_final, ".pred_class_final", "Final model")

# Combine them with patchwork
cm_all <- wrap_plots(cm_sr, cm_te, cm_final, ncol = 3)
cm_all

# save figure
#ggsave(cm_all, file = paste0("./outputs/figures/conf_mat_final_full_", Sys.Date(), ".png"), height = 6, width = 18)
```

*Updated 2025-11-04*

This is the confusion matrices for the paper
Only the overlapping six sources

```{r}
make_cm_plot_sub <- function(data, pred_col, title){
  cm <- conf_mat(data %>% filter(NAT_LOC %in% sources),
                 truth = NAT_LOC, estimate = !!sym(pred_col)) %>% 
    pluck("table") %>%
    as_tibble()

  cm_lab <- cm %>%
    group_by(Truth) %>%
    mutate(
      prop = n / sum(n),
      label = ifelse(n == 0, NA, paste0(n, "\n(", scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
      Truth = factor(Truth, levels = c("SAC", "CNH", "BAT", "MIL", "DEE", "BUT")),
      Prediction = factor(Prediction, levels = c("BUT", "DEE", "MIL", "BAT", "CNH", "SAC")),
      text_col = ifelse(prop < 0.5, "black", "white")
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    droplevels()

  ggplot(cm_lab %>% filter(!is.na(Truth), !is.na(Prediction)),
         aes(x = Truth, y = Prediction, fill = prop)) +
    geom_tile(color = "gray10", alpha = 1.0) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, color = text_col), size = 4.0, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    labs(title = title, fill = "Proportion") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16)
    )
}

# Generate plots with improved titles
cm_sr_sub    <- make_cm_plot_sub(test_final, ".pred_class_sr",
                                 #expression(paste(""^87, "Sr/", ""^86, "Sr time series"))
                                 "Sr isotope time series")
cm_te_sub    <- make_cm_plot_sub(test_final, ".pred_class_te",
                                 "Trace element (Sr/Ca, Ba/Ca)")
cm_final_sub <- make_cm_plot_sub(test_final, ".pred_class_final",
                                 "Combined prediction")

# Combine with patchwork
cm_sub <- wrap_plots(cm_sr_sub, cm_te_sub, cm_final_sub, ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(
    #subtitle = paste0(Sys.Date()),
    tag_levels = "A"
  ) &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 24, color = "gray30"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "gray30"),
    rect = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(color = NA)
  )

cm_sub

# save figure
#ggsave(cm_sub, file = paste0("./outputs/conf_mat_final_sub_", Sys.Date(), ".png"), height = 6, width = 18, dpi = 300)
ggsave(cm_sub, file =here('outputs','conf_mat_final_sub.png'), height = 6, width = 18, dpi = 300)
```
